title: Model Catalog Demo - Stellar Health
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Stellar Health through the model catalog: selecting open models, benchmark results, and compatibility matrices. Discussed tradeoffs (latency vs cost), private vs hosted deployments, quantization and kernel compatibility, and security/compliance. Agreed next steps for benchmarks, security docs, and POC kickoff.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
next_steps: Ava: Send benchmark spreadsheet and raw perf traces (link) by 2026-04-01
Share SOC2 + architecture doc (Redwood security packet)
Schedule POC kickoff for week of 2026-04-06
Provide cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated options
action_items: Ava Ramirez: Share model-compatibility matrix and benchmark spreadsheet by 2026-04-01
Raj Patel: Prepare small inference benchmark run (50K tokens) and share results by 2026-04-05
Priya Singh: Provide VPC/network requirements and existing infra notes by 2026-04-02
Liam O'Connor: Compile list of compliance questions and data residency constraints by 2026-04-03
transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Ava Ramirez, I'll lead the walk-through today, Raj from our SE team will jump into benchmarks and compatibility.
[00:12] Maya (CTO): Hi Ava, hi Raj, thanks. We have Derek, Priya, and Liam on the line. Our goal is to understand whether Redwood's model catalog and Optimize tooling can get us to parity with our current self-hosted stack but cheaper and easier to operate.
[00:30] Raj (Redwood SE): Great, thanks Maya. Quick agenda - catalog overview, how we recommend open models for different tasks, benchmark highlights, and then compatibility matrices for quantization and hardware. We'll demo the Console a bit, especially model selection and perf profiles.
[00:48] Derek (ML Eng): Quick ask - we run a lot of clinical text normalization and question-answering. Latency p95 is critical for our EHR-integrated UI, we need sub 500ms for short prompts.
[01:02] Priya (Platform): Also networking, we need to keep traffic inside our VPC and ensure keys are customer-controlled.
[01:15] Liam (Security): SOC2 and audit logs are must-haves, plus KMS integration.
[01:22] Ava: Totally, we'll cover those. Starting with the catalog - think of it as a curated list of open and verified model variants. We show model family, quantization level, expected throughput, latency profiles, and a compatibility matrix which says which runtime kernels/GPUs are supported.
[01:44] Raj: (screen share) Here's the Console - model catalog tab. You can filter by task, e.g., "instr-tuning", "qa", embeddings. For Stellar's QA work I'd surface these five models - a 7B instruction-tuned, a 13B quantized 4-bit, and a higher-accuracy 70B variant for offline batch reranks.
[02:12] Derek: Do you have bench numbers for those? We care about tokens/s and p95 latency for 64 token prompts.
[02:20] Raj: Yes, slide 3 shows p95 for 64-token gen on A100 80GB, and also on cheaper H100/RTX variants, plus our hosted endpoints. Example - 13B q4_0 is ~120ms p50 and ~420ms p95 on A100 with our optimized kernels and continuous batching disabled for low-latency mode.
[02:46] Maya: That p95 looks close to our target. How stable are those numbers in multi-tenant hosted env?
[02:54] Raj: We publish performance profiles per model per tier. For hosted, we have SLO-backed tiers; in heavy multi-tenant peaks we recommend dedicated pools or pinning to reserved capacity. Also Console shows historical latency graphs so you can see variance.
[03:12] Priya: On compatibility matrices - how do you indicate kernel/hardware support?
[03:18] Raj: In the matrix each model row has columns like AVX instructions, mixed-precision, kernel monotiles, and compatible GPU drivers. We also flag models that need specific CUDA/cuBLAS minimum versions. It helps avoid compile-time failures.
[03:34] Derek: Any gotchas with q4 vs q8 and kv cache? We've seen issues where quantized models have degraded RLHF behavior or KV cache misalignment.
[03:44] Raj: Good point - we annotate models with a "KV cache stable" badge. Some older q4 recipes can lead to subtle scoring shifts, so our catalog includes recommended quantization recipes and a regression score against a human eval set. We also include a small sample test harness you can run locally.
[04:05] Liam: For private deployments - can we bring our own keys and run the control plane in our VPC?
[04:11] Ava: Yes, Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane. KMS/HSM integrations are supported; you retain key custody. Audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. We'll attach the security packet.
[04:26] Maya: How about model updates and rollouts - we can't have silent quality regressions.
[04:32] Raj: We support pinned model versions and rollout policies. Console has eval hooks - you can register a prompt set, run canary with canary ratio, measure metric deltas. If quality drops beyond threshold, automatic rollback triggers.
[04:46] Derek: Can we bring our own models (BYOM) to the catalog?
[04:51] Ava: Yes, BYOM is supported; the catalog will ingest your artifact and run a compatibility check. If it compiles to our runtime, it gets a profile and we can run a quick benchmark.
[05:04] Raj: (shows benchmark sheet) Here's an example benchmark artifact - raw traces, token counts, environment, hardware spec. We normally provide both absolute and normalized cost numbers so you can compare hosted vs dedicated per 1M tokens.
[05:23] Maya: What's the typical cost delta between hosted and dedicated? Ballpark.
[05:29] Raj: Ballpark - for steady high throughput, dedicated reserved capacity is 30-50% cheaper per token versus hosted. Hosted gives faster setup and operational overhead savings. Optimize will recommend batching and cache policies to reduce tokens by ~15% to 25% depending on workload.
[05:48] Priya: We have strict network egress rules. Does Redwood support VPC peering or private endpoints?
[05:54] Ava: Yes private endpoints and VPC peering are supported for Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we offer private links in some regions. We'll need your VPC CIDR and peering constraints.
[06:06] Liam: On compliance - do you support customer-managed logging retention policies?
[06:11] Ava: Yes, logs can be forwarded to your S3/GCS and retention is configurable. We also expose audit logs per token, per-request ID, etc.
[06:22] Derek: Can you show how the compatibility matrix looks for a 13B model quantized to q4_0 vs q8_0?
[06:29] Raj: (screen) Here - q4_0 has excellent memory reduction but requires kernel support for low-bit matmul. We mark GPU drivers and plugin versions; q8_0 is heavier but more numerically stable. We also show evaluation delta - BLEU/ROUGE/QA F1 on our test bench.
[06:55] Maya: Any real-world examples of teams switching from self-hosted to Redwood and what surprised them?
[07:02] Ava: One customer in healthcare moved to dedicated pools and saved 40% on unit costs while getting better reliability; surprise was how much the Optimize suggestions (batching + prefix cache) reduced token count.
[07:16] Priya: About the POC - we want to validate p95 latency on our traffic shape and verify KMS integration. What's the smallest POC you recommend?
[07:24] Raj: A two-week POC: ingest 1-2 representative prompt sets, run 50K token benchmark, verify network and key integration, and validate console metrics. We'll instrument end-to-end traces.
[07:37] Derek: Do you support Mirrored replicas for hot failover?
[07:41] Raj: Yes, Dedicated supports mirrored workers and autoscaling. Console can show failover events; we also have built-in fallbacks to smaller models if capacity is constrained.
[07:53] Maya: On the developer side - SDKs and API - any differences between hosted and private?
[07:59] Ava: API is consistent. SDK authentication differs - hosted uses API keys with RBAC; private can integrate SSO and SAML with your IdP.
[08:10] Liam: Let's talk about red-team scenarios - are there evals to check hallucination / safety regressions?
[08:18] Raj: We have a safety eval suite and can run it during rollouts; Console will surface regressions by prompt set. We can also add custom evals.
[08:29] Priya: How are model artifacts stored for Private? Encrypted at rest?
[08:34] Ava: Yes, encrypted at rest, customer keys optional, and you can opt for on-prem artifact storage for air-gapped setups.
[08:44] Derek: For our QA pipeline we also need reranking. Do you have recommended retriever-reranker workflows?
[08:50] Raj: We recommend pairing smaller encoder embed models for retrieval and a 13B-70B for rerank based on latency requirements. Console has built-in recipes for retrieval+rerank and shows expected cost per query.
[09:05] Maya: Ok let's move to a quick demo of selecting a model in the Console and kicking off a benchmark.
[09:11] Raj: (screen) Filter by task -> QA -> select 13B q4_0. Click run benchmark, upload prompt set, choose hardware profile. You can toggle quantization options and see estimated latency and cost.
[09:30] Derek: The UI shows "compatibility warnings" - what level of risk do those indicate?
[09:36] Raj: Warnings are graded - green means fully supported, yellow means supported with caveats (e.g., requires driver X), red is unsupported. We include recommended mitigations.
[09:49] Maya: Would you be willing to run a small ingress test with our traffic sample?
[09:53] Ava: Yes, Raj can run a benchmark if you provide the prompt set and a small sample of tokens. We'll anonymize any PHI if present.
[10:02] (long silence while screen is shared)
[10:30] Raj: Okay, kicking off a 10k token baseline run for the 13B q4_0 - this will produce p50/p95 and cost estimate.
[10:42] Priya: On the security packet - can you send the SOC2 scope and any penetration test summaries?
[10:48] Ava: We'll attach the packet and STIG/pen test summaries; note sometimes vendor names are masked in public docs, we'll provide redacted reports if needed.
[11:02] Liam: Also need SLAs - uptime and latency SLOs for Dedicated.
[11:07] Ava: Dedicated comes with SLA tiers; we'll include those in the proposal.
[11:16] Maya: One more - how frequently do you update the model catalog with new open models?
[11:21] Raj: Roughly every 2-4 weeks we add curated entries; high-request models can be onboarded on demand. We run our own eval and provide a launch profile.
[11:33] Derek: Any limitations on model size for Private? We have some 70B+ artifacts.
[11:39] Raj: Private supports up to 70B out of the box; for >70B we have partner workflows and on-prem options with model parallelism. We'll flag that for your case.
[11:52] Maya: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[11:56] Ava: Recap - we'll send the benchmark spreadsheet and raw traces, security packet, and a model-compatibility matrix. You'll provide prompt set, VPC details, and security questions. We'll schedule POC kickoff week of 2026-04-06.
[12:13] Derek: Sounds good.
[12:15] Priya: I'll get the network details and sample data together.
[12:18] Liam: I'll compile the compliance questions.
[12:21] Ava: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items and a calendar invite for the POC kickoff.
[12:30] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hears (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache), some proper nouns slightly off. Links referenced: demo deck (internal), benchmark sheet (https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/stellar - placeholder).
